items.t: Issued a memorandum to rescind all diversity, equity, and inclusion programs and celebrations at the Department of Agriculture (2025).

items.t: Said American families deserve to know their food is American, and backed the Product of USA label.

items.q: American agriculture is not just about feeding our families, but about protecting our nation and standing up to foreign adversaries who are buying our farmland, stealing our research

items.t: Co-wrote an op-ed with HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. saying federal incentives for decades promoted highly processed foods instead of prevention.
items.q: For decades, federal incentives have promoted low-quality, highly processed foods and pharmaceutical intervention instead of prevention.

record.t: Announced that 8 more meat and poultry companies had adopted USDA's voluntary Product of USA label.
record.q: Rollins today announced that 8 additional meat and poultry companies have adopted USDA’s voluntary Product of USA (POTUSA) label

record.t: Signed a memorandum of understanding with NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman to use NASA technology and research for USDA's agricultural data.
record.q: Rollins and National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Administrator Jared Isaacman signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the U.S.

record.t: Issued a statement on President Trump's executive order lifting taxes on dyed diesel for farmers and ranchers.
record.q: Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins issued a statement on President Trump’s new executive order to provide relief for our farmers and ranchers by lifting taxes on dyed-diesel.

record.t: Launched the USDA Data Modernization Plan, which she said would cut red tape for farmers and ranchers in how USDA collects agricultural data.
record.q: “This plan puts Farmers First by cutting burdensome red tape, using modern tools, and ensuring producers have a stronger voice in how USDA collects and reports agricultural data.

record.t: Announced a new agreement with the Department of Homeland Security to detect and respond to agricultural threats such as New World screwworm at the border.
record.q: The MOU further aligns our animal health mission with DHS’s border, security, and inspection authorities, so we are better positioned to detect, assess, and respond to agricultural threats like New World screwworm.

record.t: Announced USDA's $500 million FIELDS Program to expand domestic fertilizer production.
record.q: Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins outlines the USDA's $500 million FIELDS Program aimed at increasing domestic fertilizer production.

record.t: Announced payment rates for the Farmer Bridge Assistance Program, with $11 billion in one-time payments to farmers in 2026.
record.q: Rollins announced payment rates this week for the Farmer Bridge Assistance Program, with $11 billion in one-time payments going to American farmers in 2026.

record.t: Required Minnesota to conduct recertifications for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program recipients in four counties, and in a letter to Gov. Tim Walz demanded the state participate in a pilot program.
record.q: Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins is requiring Minnesota to conduct recertifications for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients in four counties

record.t: Announced a reorganization of USDA to refocus the department on supporting American farming, ranching, and forestry.
record.q: Rollins today announced the reorganization of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), refocusing its core operations to better align with its founding mission of supporting American farming, ranching, and forestry.

record.t: Announced the National Farm Security Action Plan with other Cabinet officials, including a ban on the purchase of farmland by Chinese nationals.
record.q: The Trump administration is launching an aggressive, multi-agency effort to protect America’s farmlands, food supply and critical research from influence and control by US adversaries — including banning the purchase of farmland by Chinese nationals.

record.t: Was confirmed by the U.S. Senate as Secretary of Agriculture by a vote of 72 to 28.
record.q: Nomination Description: Brooke Rollins, of Texas, to be Secretary of Agriculture Vote Counts: YEAs 72 NAYs 28
